description: Polyxd semantic component catalog: when to use each component, accessibility and agent requirements, rendering rules and platform mappings. Generated file.

Action.summary: A button that triggers a host capability.
whenToUse: Anything the user can do that isn't typing or choosing
whenNotToUse: Navigating between views: use Views
Confirming something destructive: wrap in Confirm

accessibility.role: button
requirements: Label describes the outcome
Target at least size.target.min
Disabled actions explain why nearby

rendering: At most one primary action visible at a time
danger tone uses color.action.danger.*
'description' sits under the label in type.body.small, muted; the button's accessible description
ui.copy is handled by the renderer: it copies 'copy' (or the context's 'text') and announces 'Copied' politely

ActionBar.summary: The set of actions for a surface or section; the renderer places it where that platform expects.
whenToUse: Two or more actions that apply to the whole surface or section
whenNotToUse: A single action inline with content: use Action directly

accessibility.role: toolbar / group
requirements: Order in the accessibility tree is order of importance

rendering: Web: bottom of the section, primary last on desktop and first on mobile stacks
iOS/Android: toolbar or bottom bar on compact screens
sources: Platform conventions for action placement (Jakob's law)

ActionMenu.summary: Secondary actions behind one control: an overflow menu, a dropdown, a split button or a context menu.
whenToUse: Three or more secondary actions on a row, a card or a page header
One usual action with rarer alternatives (split: 'Save' with 'Save as draft')
Actions that belong to the thing under the pointer (context)
whenNotToUse: One or two actions: use Action or ActionBar, where they are visible
The main thing to do on the surface: never hidden in a menu
Navigation between views: use Views or Navigation

accessibility.role: a menu button (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded) opening a menu of menuitems; a split's main part is a plain button
requirements: Every action is reachable by keyboard: arrows move, Enter activates, Escape closes and returns focus
An overflow control is named for what it holds ('More actions for Acme Corp'), never just '…'
A context menu's actions are also reachable another way (an overflow control), since right-click and long-press aren't discoverable

ActionMenu.agent: Opens the menu by its name and activates an action by its label.
rendering: The menu uses color.surface.overlay with elevation.overlay and radius.default; items are size.control.default tall with space.inset.default
A danger-toned Action shows in color.status.danger.emphasis after a divider
The overflow control is an icon-only button at size.target.min with the label as its accessible name; a dropdown shows the label with a chevron
A split's two parts share one outline; the menu part is at least size.target.min wide

mappings.web: shadcn DropdownMenu, ContextMenu; split as a ButtonGroup

Card.summary: One self-contained entity (an account, an order, a place), optionally actionable as a whole.
whenToUse: Items in a Collection that each represent an entity
A single entity summary in a larger surface
whenNotToUse: Plain grouping: use Group
Tabular data with many attributes: use Table

accessibility.role: article (or link/button when it has an action)
requirements: Title is the accessible name
When actionable, the title is the card's one link; controls inside it (a Toggle, an Action) stay separate targets with their own names

Card.agent: Activate the card by its title; use controls inside it by their own labels.
rendering: If 'action' is set, the whole card opens it; controls in children (e.g. a habit's done Toggle) sit above that target and act on their own
Uses surface.raised and radius.default
'progress' renders a progress bar with its label or percentage

mappings.ios: GroupBox, or a Button/NavigationLink with card styling in lists
mappings.android: Card / ElevatedCard / OutlinedCard (onClick variant when actionable)

Chart.summary: A visual summary of data, always paired with a text summary.
whenToUse: A trend, comparison, share or spread matters more than exact values
whenNotToUse: Exact values matter most: use Table or Metric
A single number: use Metric

accessibility.role: img (figure) with the summary as description, plus a data-table alternative
requirements: 'summary' states the takeaway in words
Series are distinguishable without color (labels, markers)
The underlying data is available as a table

Chart.agent: Reads the summary, and the data through the table alternative.
rendering: trend → line, comparison → bar, composition → stacked bar (pie only for ≤ 4 parts), distribution → histogram

relationship → scatter (x is a measure too), flow → stacked flows from each x value to each series, hierarchy → treemap of the first series, matrix → heatmap of x values by series, range → bars from the first series to the second
Series colors use color.data.categorical.N in order; a matrix shades one color by value and prints the value in each cell

mappings.android: Third-party (e.g. Vico) or Canvas; no built-in M3 chart

Chart.a2ui: No equivalent in the Basic catalog; exports as Text(summary) + List
sources: Data visualization: choosing the form by intent

Choice.summary: Pick one or several options from a known set. The renderer chooses the control.
whenToUse: Any choice from a known set of options
whenNotToUse: On/off setting: use Toggle
Picking between rich entities by comparing attributes: use Comparison

accessibility.role: radiogroup / group of checkboxes / listbox / combobox (depends on rendering)
requirements: Visible group label
Every option has a text label

rendering: single, 2–4 short options → segmented control or radios
single, 5–10 → radios (or select on compact screens)
single, > 10 → searchable select
multiple, ≤ 10 → checkboxes; > 10 → searchable multi-select
Option order comes from host data or remembers the last order used

mappings.web: shadcn ToggleGroup / RadioGroup / Select / Combobox (Command + Popover) / Checkbox
mappings.android: SegmentedButton / RadioButton rows / ExposedDropdownMenuBox / Checkbox rows

Code.summary: Code, a command or preformatted text, shown as written and copyable.
whenToUse: A command to run, a snippet to paste, an identifier to copy
Structured text whose spacing matters
whenNotToUse: Prose: use Text
Something the person types: use TextInput

accessibility.role: region named by the label, holding a code element; the copy control is a button named 'Copy <label>'
requirements: Text is real text: selectable and read by screen readers line by line
Copying is announced ('Copied')
A secret is masked with the same length, with a 'Show' control

Code.agent: Reads the text verbatim; can activate Copy.
rendering: type.mono at type.body.small on color.surface.subtle, with radius.control
Overflow scrolls sideways unless wrap is set; never clipped
The copy control sits in the top-right corner and says 'Copied' for two seconds after use

mappings.web: pre > code with a Copy button
mappings.ios: Text with monospaced design in a rounded rectangle
mappings.android: Text with FontFamily.Monospace in a Surface

CodeInput.summary: A one-time code or PIN, typed into one box per character.
whenToUse: A verification code from email or SMS
A PIN or a short recovery code
whenNotToUse: A password: the host's own sign-in flow, never a generated screen
Any text longer than twelve characters: use TextInput

accessibility.role: a group named by the label; one text input per character, each named 'Digit N of M'
requirements: Typing moves focus forward; Backspace moves it back; pasting the whole code fills every box
The numeric kind opens the numeric keyboard and accepts autofill of one-time codes
Errors are said against the group, not one box

CodeInput.agent: Reads the label and length; enters the code.
rendering: Boxes are size.control.large squares with radius.control, type.heading.small, centred, in type.mono
The active box shows color.border.focus; a filled box shows color.border.strong
Boxes are grouped in threes or fours by a wider gap past six characters

Collection.summary: A list of items from host data, each rendered with the same template.
whenToUse: Browsing a set of similar entities
Search results
whenNotToUse: Attributes compared across items: use Table or Comparison
Choosing an option in a form: use Choice

accessibility.role: list / listitem (listbox when selectable)
requirements: Announces the item count
An empty state is provided

Collection.agent: Items are enumerated with their titles; each item exposes its own actions.
rendering: Long lists are virtualized by the renderer
Items keep their order from host data
grid: 2 columns on phones, more as width allows; list: one item per row
auto: grid when the item template is a Card with media, otherwise list
'timeline' marks each item on a line, newest first, for activity feeds
'carousel' scrolls horizontally with snap points, Previous and Next buttons and an 'N of M' readout; every item stays reachable by keyboard
'calendar' is a month grid with the items on their days; Previous and Next move a month at a time
Paging shows items per page, the range and the total, as a Table does
Selection shows the bulk-action bar, naming how many items are selected, while any are
reorderable: a drag handle per item, plus Move up / Move down buttons; the new order is written to 'order'

mappings.web: List markup with Card or row template; ScrollArea for long lists

sources: Hick's law: filter before long lists

ColorInput.summary: Pick a colour: from swatches the host offers, or any colour.
whenToUse: A colour for a label, a tag, a calendar, a theme
Choosing from a set of brand colours
whenNotToUse: A choice that happens to be shown as colours (a plan, a size): use Choice

accessibility.role: swatches are a radiogroup of radios named by their labels; the free picker is a native color input plus a text field for the value
requirements: Every swatch has a name; colour alone is never the only identification
The value is editable as text, so it can be typed and read
The chosen colour is shown beside its text value

ColorInput.agent: Reads the swatch names; picks one by name or types a value.
rendering: Swatches are size.control.default squares with radius.control and a 1px color.border.default ring; the chosen one shows color.border.focus
The free picker is the platform's, with the text value beside it in type.mono

mappings.web: input type=color + Radix RadioGroup for swatches

Comparison.summary: Compare a few options across the same attributes, and choose one.
whenToUse: Choosing between 2–4 plans, products, routes or offers
whenNotToUse: More than ~5 items: use Table with sorting
No decision needed: use Table

accessibility.role: table (items as columns on wide screens) or list of cards
requirements: Attribute names are headers
'better' is conveyed in text, not only color

Comparison.agent: Reads attributes per item; choose actions are named with the item title.
rendering: Wide: items as columns; compact: one card per item with the same attribute order
Best values per attribute are marked when 'better' is set
Exactly one item may be recommended; its badge carries recommendedReason
Attributes with the same group sit under one heading
Boolean values render as a check or a dash with text alternatives ('Included' / 'Not included')
On compact surfaces the recommended item comes first

mappings.ios: Grid / Table on regular width; List of GroupBox on compact
mappings.android: LazyRow of Cards or Column of Cards

Comparison.a2ui: No direct equivalent; exports as List of Card

Confirm.summary: Asks the user to confirm a consequential or destructive action, showing what will happen.
whenToUse: Moving money, deleting data, sending on someone's behalf, anything irreversible
whenNotToUse: Routine reversible actions (prefer undo)
Information only: use Status

accessibility.role: alertdialog
requirements: Focus starts on the least destructive option
Confirm label repeats the action verb
Escape cancels

Confirm.agent: Reads title and consequence; confirm and cancel are named buttons.
rendering: destructive uses color.action.danger.*
Capabilities with high risk level must use Confirm (enforced by the verifier)
the consequence sits directly above the confirm button
amount and subject lead the dialog when set
consequences render as an icon list, two columns on wide surfaces

DateInput.summary: A date, time, date-time or date range.
whenToUse: Any date or time entry
whenNotToUse: Relative choices like 'This month / Last month': use Choice

accessibility.role: group of spinbuttons or a date picker dialog
requirements: Typing the date is always possible, not only picking from a calendar

DateInput.agent: Fill by label with an ISO date.
rendering: Memorable dates (birthdays) use separate day/month/year fields; near dates use a calendar
'month' and 'year' take only that part; the year field is typed, four digits
multiple: each chosen date becomes a chip with a remove control; the field adds another

DetailList.summary: Label/value pairs describing one thing (a summary, a receipt, a review step).
whenToUse: Reviewing before submitting
Showing the attributes of one entity
Receipts
Fees, prices and totals before someone commits (variant 'receipt')
whenNotToUse: Many entities with the same attributes: use Table
Comparing entities: use Comparison

accessibility.role: list of term/definition pairs (dl)
requirements: Label and value are programmatically associated

DetailList.agent: Read each label with its value.
rendering: Keeps the item order stable across generations (keys are remembered)
receipt: values right-aligned in tabular figures, the total row emphasised; people read amounts from the right
'grid' lays fields out in columns by width, label above value
rowAction: each row ends with a 'Change' link whose accessible name includes the row's label; the total row has none

mappings.ios: LabeledContent rows in a Form/List section

Disclosure.summary: Progressive disclosure: secondary content hidden behind a toggle.
whenToUse: Details most people don't need (fees breakdown, advanced options, help text)
whenNotToUse: Content everyone needs to complete the task
Primary navigation

accessibility.role: button (aria-expanded) + region
requirements: Summary is a button with expanded state
Hidden content is not in the tab order while closed

Disclosure.agent: Expand by the summary text; state is exposed as expanded/collapsed.
rendering: Never hide required inputs or the primary action inside a closed Disclosure

mappings.android: Expandable ListItem / AnimatedVisibility with a toggle row

Disclosure.a2ui: No direct equivalent; exports as Column (content always shown)

FileInput.summary: Choose or drop files to attach or upload.
whenToUse: Attaching a document, a receipt, a photo
Importing a file the product reads
whenNotToUse: Taking a photo with the camera: the host's own flow
Pasting text: use TextInput

accessibility.role: a native file input, labelled; the drop zone is a large target for the same input
requirements: Keyboard opens the chooser; drag-and-drop is an addition, never the only way
Chosen files are listed as text with a 'Remove <name>' button each
Type and size limits are said before choosing and in any refusal

FileInput.agent: Reads the label and limits; attaches files through the host.
rendering: A dashed drop zone on color.surface.subtle with radius.control, the chooser control inside it
Each chosen file shows name, size and a remove control; a progress bar while the host uploads
Refusals use color.status.danger text under the zone

mappings.web: shadcn Input type=file with a drop zone

FilterPanel.summary: Filters for a list of results, with the result count.
whenToUse: Browsing results people narrow by several attributes
More than two filters, or filters that take space (ranges, long lists)
whenNotToUse: One or two quick filters: put a Choice (chips) above the results
Filling in information: use Form

accessibility.role: region (filters) plus the results
requirements: The result count is announced politely when it changes
Each active filter can be removed with a named button ('Remove filter: Desk')

FilterPanel.agent: Set filter inputs by label; read the result count; remove filters by their Remove buttons.
rendering: Wide: filters in a sidebar beside the results
Compact: a 'Filters · n' button opens a bottom sheet whose action says 'Show n results'
Active filters show as removable chips above the results
Filters apply as they change (no separate Apply on wide)

Form.summary: Collects inputs and submits them together.
whenToUse: Any set of inputs that are submitted together
whenNotToUse: Settings that apply immediately: use Toggles with actions
Several distinct stages: use Steps

accessibility.role: form
requirements: Submit is a real submit button
On submit errors, focus moves to an error summary that links to each field

Form.agent: Fill fields by label, then activate the submit button by its label.
rendering: One column; labels above fields
Submit is the primary action; cancel is secondary
Submit context is built from the form's input bindings
'horizontal' becomes stacked on compact surfaces
'aside' sits beside the form on wide surfaces; on compact ones it comes first, before the fields, so people read what they are agreeing to

mappings.android: Column of fields + Button (no Form primitive)

sources: GOV.UK question pages and error summary

Group.summary: Visually groups closely related items without a heading (proximity).
whenToUse: A few items that belong together (a key figure and its caption, several metrics)
whenNotToUse: The group needs a heading: use Section
Choosing between items: use Choice or Comparison

accessibility.role: group
requirements: Has an accessible name when it contains interactive items

Group.agent: Treated as one unit when its label is present.
rendering: 'inline' collapses to a stack below the compact breakpoint
Gap uses space.stack.default or space.inline.default

mappings.web: <div role=group> with flex/grid and semantic spacing tokens

Identity.summary: A person, team or organisation: picture, name and details, or several of them together.
whenToUse: Who something belongs to, was sent by or is assigned to
The recipient on a payment, the owner on a record, the members on a team
A list of people where the face helps recognition
whenNotToUse: Choosing a person from a list: use Choice with avatarPath
A person's full record: use Card or DetailList

accessibility.role: group named by the name; the picture is decorative and the name is text
requirements: The name is real text, never only an image or initials
A group's accessible name lists the first names and how many more
With an action, the whole element is one button or link named by the name

Identity.agent: Reads the name and detail; a group exposes every member's name.
rendering: Initials come from the name's first letters, on a neutral surface with color.text.default; a pack may derive a stable colour from the name
Sizes: small 24px, default 40px, large 64px; the name uses type.body.default or type.heading.small for large
A group overlaps pictures by a quarter, with a '+N' tag for the rest
Images are never stretched; missing images fall back to initials, never to a broken image

Media.summary: An image, video, audio clip, gallery or QR code supplied by the host.
whenToUse: Photos or illustrations that help identify something (a product, a place, a person)
A recording people play, or a code they scan
whenNotToUse: Decoration with no information
Icons for actions (renderer supplies those)

accessibility.role: img (video / audio players, list for a gallery)
requirements: Has alt text unless decorative (then hidden from assistive technology)
Video and audio have native controls and offer a transcript
A QR code's alt says what scanning it does

Media.agent: Reads the alt text; a gallery's images by their own alt text; a QR code's value.
rendering: Images never convey information that is not also in text
'video' shows 'poster' until played; 'audio' is a compact player; both put 'transcript' under a disclosure
'gallery' is a grid of the items' images, each with its own alt text
'qr' is drawn on a canvas at a size that scans from a phone, with the alt as its accessible name
Media.a2ui: Image (video, audio and gallery export as Image + Text; a QR code as Text of its value)

Metric.summary: A key figure with a label, and optionally its change.
whenToUse: One to four headline numbers the user asked about
whenNotToUse: Many numbers: use Table or DetailList
Trends over time: use Chart

accessibility.role: group (label + value)
requirements: Change direction is conveyed in text as well as color
Screen readers read label, value and change as one sentence

rendering: Value uses type.numeric.display
Change uses color.data.positive / negative according to 'favorable'

mappings.web: Card-like block with semantic tokens (no dedicated shadcn primitive)
mappings.ios: LabeledContent or a VStack; Gauge for bounded values

whenToUse: Software with sections people move between (B2B apps, dashboards)
Only when the host doesn't already provide navigation
whenNotToUse: Steps of one task: use Steps
Sections of one record: use Views
A surface embedded in a host that has its own navigation

accessibility.role: navigation
requirements: The current item carries aria-current="page"
Badges say what they count ('12 overdue')

Navigation.agent: Move between sections by activating items by their labels.
rendering: Wide: a side navigation with grouped items
Compact: a menu button that opens the navigation
Badges sit at the end of their item
'breadcrumb' is an ordered trail ending with the current item (aria-current="page"), never behind a menu button
'nested' shows each group as an expandable section; the group holding the current item starts open
'toc' lists the page's sections as anchors, the section in view highlighted
'local' lays the items out as tabs, the current one marked

mappings.ios: TabView or a sidebar on iPad

sources: NN/g: navigation should show where you are

Panel.summary: Content over the current view: a dialog, a drawer, a bottom sheet or a popover, opened from an action and dismissed to return.
whenToUse: A short task on top of the page: edit one thing, pick one thing, see one record
Detail the person asked for that shouldn't replace where they are
A small set of options next to the control that opened them (popover)
whenNotToUse: Confirming a consequential action: use Confirm, which is a dialog with the right words and order
A whole flow of several steps: use Steps on its own surface
Passing feedback: use Status

accessibility.role: dialog (aria-modal for dialog, drawer and sheet) named by the title; popover is a non-modal dialog
requirements: Focus moves into the panel on open and back to the opener on close
Tab stays inside a modal panel; Escape dismisses a dismissible one
The page behind a modal panel is inert
A sheet can be dismissed by dragging down as well as by the close control

Panel.agent: Opens, reads the content and closes it by name; the footer actions are exposed like any ActionBar.
rendering: A backdrop of color.surface.inverse at opacity.overlay for modal kinds

dialog: max 560px on desktop, full width with space.inset.default on phones; drawer: 420px from the end edge; sheet: from the bottom with radius.large on the top corners; popover: color.surface.overlay with elevation.overlay and an arrow
The title is type.heading.medium with the close control at the end of the header
The action bar sits in a footer; on phones it is fixed to the bottom, full width
Motion uses motion.duration.default and motion.easing.standard; reduced motion fades instead

Progress.summary: How far along something is, or how much of a bounded amount is used: a bar, a ring or a meter.
whenToUse: A task that takes time, with a known share done
How much of a quota, budget or capacity is used
Progress towards a goal (pages read, steps walked)
whenNotToUse: A number the person came to see: use Metric
Steps of a task the person moves through: use Steps
A short wait with nothing to measure: Status 'loading'

accessibility.role: progressbar (bar, ring) or meter, named by the label, with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext
requirements: The readout is real text next to the graphic, never only the fill
A meter's tone is also said in text ('nearly full'), not only shown by colour
Indeterminate progress has no value attributes and is announced as busy

Progress.agent: Reads label, value and max as text.
rendering: The track uses color.surface.subtle; the fill uses color.action.primary.background, or color.status.<tone>.emphasis for a toned meter
Height is size.control.small / 3 for a bar; a ring is size.control.default across
Readout in tabular figures, type.body.small, after the label
The bar's length means the fraction: never used for an amount with no bound

mappings.web: shadcn Progress; meter as a native <meter>

RangeInput.summary: A number, or a range between two numbers, within known bounds.
whenToUse: Approximate values within a range (budget cap, volume)
A price or date range for filtering (mode 'range')
whenNotToUse: Exact values: use TextInput with kind 'number' or 'currency'

accessibility.role: slider
requirements: Current value is shown as text
Keyboard arrows change the value by step

RangeInput.agent: Set the value directly by label.
rendering: Shows min, max and the current formatted value
mode 'range' shows two thumbs and min/max fields that stay in sync

Rating.summary: A score out of N: given by the person, or shown as others gave it.
whenToUse: Asking how something went, out of five
Showing a product's or place's rating with the count behind it
whenNotToUse: A number within bounds that isn't a score: use RangeInput
Yes or no: use Toggle or Choice

accessibility.role: radiogroup of radios named '1 star' to 'N stars' when it can be given; an image named '4.6 out of 5' when read-only
requirements: Every star is a real control at size.target.min when the person can rate
The current value is announced; half values are said as such
Read-only ratings carry the score as text, not only as filled shapes

Rating.agent: Reads the score and the count; sets a score by choosing '<n> stars'.
rendering: Filled shapes use color.status.warning.emphasis; empty ones use color.border.default
The readout ('4.6') is shown after the shapes in tabular figures, with the count in color.text.muted
A rating that can be given shows the label above, like every input

Section.summary: A titled region of the surface that groups related content under a heading.
whenToUse: The surface has two or more distinct topics (e.g. 'Recipient' and 'Amount')
Content would otherwise exceed one screen and needs signposting
whenNotToUse: Only one topic: put content directly under the root
Visual grouping without a heading: use Group

accessibility.role: region (with heading)
requirements: Title is rendered as a real heading; nesting depth sets the heading level
Title is the region's accessible name

Section.agent: Navigate by heading; the title names the region.
rendering: Heading level follows nesting depth, never chosen by the model
Spacing between sections uses space.stack.section

mappings.web: <section> + heading; shadcn has no Section primitive (plain markup with semantic tokens)
mappings.ios: Section(header:) inside List/Form, or VStack with .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) on the title
mappings.android: Column with a Text heading marked Modifier.semantics { heading() }

Section.a2ui: No direct equivalent; exports as Column with a Text(variant: h2) first child

Status.summary: Feedback about state: info, success, warning, error, empty or loading.
whenToUse: Results of an action
Empty collections
Errors with a way to recover
Loading states
'undo': after a reversible action ran, say what happened and offer Undo instead of asking first
whenNotToUse: Validation errors on a field: inputs show their own errors
Confirmation before acting: use Confirm

accessibility.role: status or alert (live region)
requirements: success/info/loading are polite live regions; error is assertive
Meaning is in text, not only color or icon

Status.agent: Reads the title and message; the recovery action is exposed.
rendering: error and warning use color.status.* tokens and an icon
empty states explain why and what to do next
loading shows a skeleton when layout is known, otherwise a progress indicator
'undo' renders as a snackbar at the bottom of the surface, announced politely, with the Undo action
Empty states may carry an ActionBar: one primary and one secondary action
'inline' renders a bordered notice with its action on the right

mappings.android: Snackbar / Card with status color / CircularProgressIndicator

sources: Nielsen: visibility of system status; help users recover from errors

Steps.summary: A task split into ordered steps with visible progress.
whenToUse: Tasks with dependent stages or too many inputs for one view (checkout, onboarding)
whenNotToUse: Independent views: use Views
Under ~6 inputs: a single Form

accessibility.role: group with step progress (aria-current on the current step)
requirements: Current step and total are announced
Back never loses entered data

Steps.agent: Reads 'step N of M'; next/back are exposed as buttons.
rendering: Renderer provides Back (ui.back) and Next (ui.next); the last step shows 'finish'
Each step validates before moving on
'tasklist' is a list of tasks with a status tag each (GOV.UK task list); a task opens its content in place, and 'finish' follows the list, saying how many are done
'guide' shows every step's title and content in a numbered list, with 'finish' after the last

mappings.web: Progress + step content (no shadcn stepper primitive)
mappings.ios: NavigationStack pushes or a paged view with a ProgressView

Steps.a2ui: No direct equivalent; exports as Column of the current step

Table.summary: Tabular data: many items sharing the same attributes.
whenToUse: Scanning or comparing many rows by several attributes
Records people scan, sort, select and act on in bulk (B2B lists)
whenNotToUse: One entity: use DetailList
A few entities where the user must choose: use Comparison

accessibility.role: table with caption and column headers
requirements: Has a caption
Column headers are real header cells
Numeric columns are right-aligned by format
Sortable headers carry aria-sort and say what sorting does
The select-all checkbox is mixed when some rows are selected
The bulk-action bar names how many rows are selected, announced politely
Each row's action menu is named after its row

Table.agent: Read by row and column headers; rows with rowAction are activatable. Sort by activating a column header; select rows by their checkboxes; act in bulk from the bar that appears.
rendering: On compact screens, rows become stacked cards with label/value pairs
Alignment follows the column format, never chosen by the model
Numbers and currency are right-aligned with tabular figures; 'status' renders as a tag using 'tones'
On compact surfaces the table becomes a list of rows: the entity, the key fields in one line, and the status
Selection replaces the toolbar with the bulk-action bar while rows are selected
Paging shows rows per page, the range and the total
expandable: each row starts with a toggle (aria-expanded) named after the row; the open row's 'detail' spans the table beneath it

mappings.web: shadcn Table (optionally Data Table with TanStack)
mappings.ios: Table on regular width; List of rows on compact width
mappings.android: LazyColumn of rows with a header row (no built-in M3 table)

Table.a2ui: No direct equivalent; exports as List of Row

Tag.summary: A short label, status or count attached to something else.
whenToUse: The state of a record, next to its name: 'Past due', 'Draft', 'Live'
A category or label a thing carries
How many of something, on a navigation item or a section heading
Chosen items a person can take off again
whenNotToUse: A whole sentence of feedback: use Status
Something the person switches on or off: use Toggle
A metric the person came for: use Metric

accessibility.role: text; for 'count', the label is the accessible name of the number; for a removable tag, a button named 'Remove <label>'
requirements: Tone is conveyed by the label, never only by colour
A count reads as '<label>: <count>' to a screen reader
The remove control is at least size.target.min and named for what it removes

Tag.agent: Reads label, tone and count; can activate the remove control by its name.
rendering: status uses color.status.<tone>.background and .foreground; label and count use neutral tokens
count is set in tabular figures
A tag never wraps: long labels are truncated with the full text on hover and in the accessible name
Fits inline with text and in a Card header; radius.small unless the pack sets a pill

whenToUse: Explanations, instructions, messages
whenNotToUse: Headings: use Section title
Label/value pairs: use DetailList
Key figures: use Metric

accessibility.role: text
requirements: Body text is at least 16px (type.body.default)
Line length is capped by measure.max

rendering: 'supporting' uses color.text.muted
No inline styling; emphasis comes from structure
'rich' renders only the four markup forms, as real elements; anything else, including HTML, is shown as typed, and only http, https, mailto and tel links are live
'list' renders a ul or ol; entries are shown as text, or by 'itemPath' when they are objects
'quote' is a blockquote, the cite on its own line after it
format 'color' shows a swatch of the value beside it; 'bytes' shows a size like 1.2 MB

TextInput.summary: A single text-like value: text, number, email, phone, currency, search or long text.
whenToUse: Free-form values the user types
whenNotToUse: A value from a known set: use Choice
Dates: use DateInput
Secrets (passwords, card numbers): not generated; hosts provide their own secure flows

accessibility.role: textbox / searchbox / spinbutton
requirements: Visible label, never placeholder-only
Help and errors are associated with the field
Kind sets the right keyboard and autocomplete

rendering: Width suggests expected length
Errors appear after the user leaves the field or submits, not while typing
kind 'search' renders as a pill search field with an icon; the label stays as its accessible name
size 'hero' renders a large centred amount with the currency symbol dimmed
'suggestions' and 'mentions' are comboboxes: the list opens as you type, arrow keys move through it, Enter takes an option, Escape closes it
'richtext' is an editable area with Bold, Italic and List controls; the value is text with **bold**, *italic* and '- ' items
'tags' shows each value as a chip with a remove control; Enter or a comma adds what was typed, Backspace in an empty field removes the last chip; the value is a list of strings
'code' uses type.numeric (monospace) and turns off autocorrect, autocapitalize and spellcheck
'masked' fills the mask's literal characters as you type and stores the text as shown
'inline' renders the value as text with an Edit control; Enter saves, Escape restores the previous value

mappings.web: shadcn Input / Textarea with Label and FormMessage

sources: GOV.UK text input and question pages

whenToUse: Settings that take effect immediately
A single yes/no inside a form
whenNotToUse: Choosing between named options: use Choice

accessibility.role: switch (immediate) / checkbox (in a form)
requirements: Label says what 'on' means

Toggle.agent: Toggle by label; state is exposed as on/off.
rendering: With 'action' it renders as a switch; inside a Form without action, as a checkbox
sources: Nielsen: match between system and the real world

Tree.summary: A hierarchy people expand, browse and pick from: folders, an org chart, nested categories.
whenToUse: Things that contain things: folders and files, an organisation, nested categories
Picking a place in a hierarchy (move to folder, choose a category)
whenNotToUse: A flat list, however long: use Collection or Table
Nested navigation of the product itself: use Navigation
Progressive disclosure of one section: use Disclosure

accessibility.role: tree with treeitem nodes; aria-expanded on nodes with children, aria-selected when selectable
requirements: Arrow keys move and expand; Home and End jump; typing jumps to a label
Level and position are exposed (aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset)
Expanded state is announced; selection is announced

Tree.agent: Reads every node by label and level; expands a node by name and selects or activates one by name.
rendering: Indent per level uses space.inline.default; the expander is a chevron at size.target.min
Leaves have no expander and align with siblings' labels
Selection uses color.selection.background; the focused node shows color.border.focus
Beyond 200 nodes the renderer virtualises rows

Views.summary: Switch between alternative views of the same subject (tabs).
whenToUse: 2–6 peer views of the same data (Overview / Transactions / Settings)
whenNotToUse: Sequential steps: use Steps
Filtering one list: use Choice

accessibility.role: tablist / tab / tabpanel
requirements: Each tab has a visible label
Arrow keys move between tabs

Views.agent: Select a view by its label.
rendering: More than 4 views on compact screens become a menu or scrollable tabs
Counts sit beside their labels and are part of the tab's accessible name

mappings.ios: Picker(.segmented) switching content, or TabView for top-level
